candidates.name: Beau Bayh
candidates.gradeNote: No public positions found on life, marriage, religious liberty or guns; did not answer the iVoterGuide questionnaire, which rates him 'Liberal' based on public data, and he is endorsed by Democrat Pete Buttigieg. His stated priorities are an independent audit of the office, protecting early voting, citizen-led ballot initiatives and ending straight-ticket voting.
candidates.description: Indianapolis attorney, former U.S. Marine Corps captain and son of former Gov. and Sen. Evan Bayh, nominated at the June 2026 Democratic convention.

candidates.name: Max Engling
candidates.gradeNote: On the iVoterGuide questionnaire he strongly agreed that life deserves legal protection from conception, that marriage is one man and one woman, and that no one should be compelled to provide services against religious beliefs; he also supports photo voter ID and signed the Americans for Tax Reform Taxpayer Protection Pledge. He has no voting record, and President Trump endorsed him in October 2026.
candidates.description: Former U.S. House Republican staffer and regional director for Sen. Jim Banks who defeated incumbent Diego Morales for the Republican nomination at the June 2026 convention.

candidates.name: Lauri A. Shillings
candidates.gradeNote: Her campaign focuses on cutting red tape, modernizing business filings, campaign-finance transparency and neutral election administration; she states no positions on life, marriage, religious liberty or guns. She did not answer the iVoterGuide questionnaire, which rates her 'Moderate.'
candidates.description: Chair of the Hamilton County Libertarian Party and creative director at the University of Indianapolis, running as the Libertarian nominee.

candidates.name: Greg Ballard
candidates.gradeNote: As Indianapolis mayor in 2015 he publicly denounced Indiana's Religious Freedom Restoration Act and urged lawmakers to add sexual orientation and gender identity to state civil rights protections. He did not answer the iVoterGuide questionnaire, which rates him 'Liberal' based on public data.
candidates.description: Former two-term Republican mayor of Indianapolis (2008-2015) and retired Marine lieutenant colonel, running as an independent on the Lincoln Party line.

candidates.name: Jessica Bailey
candidates.gradeNote: No public positions found on life, marriage, religious liberty or guns; she did not answer the iVoterGuide questionnaire, which rates her 'Liberal' based on public data. On fiscal issues she opposes eliminating property and gas taxes, says she would not raise taxes without debate, and wants a more accessible state transparency portal.
candidates.description: Two-term Porter County Circuit Court clerk and former Portage Township school board member, running as the Democratic nominee.

candidates.name: Elise Nieshalla
candidates.gradeNote: In office she voted in March 2025 for a non-ESG investment policy for the state's Hoosier START retirement plan and chairs a state financial officers' national-debt task force. On the iVoterGuide questionnaire she supports protecting life from conception, one-man-one-woman marriage, constitutional carry, religious-conscience protections and parental rights; she is endorsed by the Indiana Republican Assembly.
candidates.description: Incumbent Republican comptroller appointed in 2023, former Boone County Council president and former Indiana Department of Commerce economic development manager.

candidates.name: John Schick
candidates.gradeNote: His only public positions found are from a 2022 interview: reduce government spending, cut regulations, and keep the auditor independent of the governing party. He did not answer the 2026 surveys from the Capital Chronicle or iVoterGuide, which rates him 'Insufficient Information.'
candidates.description: Chesterton business consultant and former Libertarian Party state treasurer, running his third or fourth campaign for comptroller/auditor.

candidates.name: Coumba Kebe
candidates.gradeNote: She questions whether Indiana's anti-ESG investment efforts served taxpayers, opposes eliminating property and gas taxes, and says government should not make decisions 'just focused on the numbers.' She did not answer the iVoterGuide questionnaire, which rates her 'Liberal' based on public data; no positions were found on life, marriage, religious liberty or guns.
candidates.description: Health care executive and founder of Scope Consulting, which serves home care agencies, running as the Democratic nominee after losing a Democratic primary for Indiana House District 29.

candidates.name: Daniel Elliott
candidates.gradeNote: As treasurer he put BlackRock on an ESG watchlist in 2024 and, as an INPRS board member, voted to replace it as manager of a roughly $969 million portfolio. On the iVoterGuide questionnaire he supports defunding Planned Parenthood, opposes elective abortion except to save the mother's life, backs one-man-one-woman marriage, wants no new gun restrictions and supports religious-conscience protections and parental rights.
candidates.description: Incumbent Republican state treasurer first elected in 2022, former Morgan County Council member and software engineer/consultant.

candidates.name: Frank J. Mrvan
candidates.gradeNote: SBA Pro-Life America grade F; Heritage Action 119th Congress score 0%; LCV lifetime score 97%. Voted for the 2022 Respect for Marriage Act, against the 2023 Born-Alive Abortion Survivors Protection Act (did not vote on the 2025 version), and against the 2025 Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act; campaign platform supports codifying Roe v. Wade.
candidates.description: Hammond native and former North Township trustee seeking a fourth term in the U.S. House.

candidates.name: Barb Regnitz
candidates.gradeNote: Newcomer to federal office; campaign site pledges to defend the right to keep and bear arms, strengthen border security, end reckless spending and reduce the national debt, and keep girls' sports and facilities for biological females. No public position on abortion found (left the iVoterGuide Right to Life item unanswered); endorsed by President Trump, Sens. Banks and Young, and Maggie's List.
candidates.description: Porter County commissioner (elected 2022) with a background in software engineering and financial planning.

candidates.name: Jamee Decio
candidates.gradeNote: Campaign platform calls for eliminating ICE's budget and disbanding the agency, a pathway to citizenship, and much higher taxes on billionaires; no stated positions on abortion, marriage, religious liberty or firearms were found.
candidates.description: South Bend attorney and former Elkhart County deputy prosecutor.

candidates.name: Rudy Yakym
candidates.gradeNote: SBA Pro-Life America A+; Heritage Action 119th Congress score 85%; LCV lifetime 1%. Voted against the 2022 Respect for Marriage Act and for the Born-Alive Abortion Survivors Protection Act (2023 and 2025) and the 2025 Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act.
candidates.description: Republican who has represented Indiana's 2nd District since 2022, campaigning on limited government, lower taxes and reduced regulation.

candidates.name: William Eric Henry
candidates.gradeNote: Told the Capital Chronicle he supports any reduction in taxes at all levels and downsizing government, and lists medical freedom and privacy as priorities; also backs federal cannabis reform. No stated positions on abortion, marriage, religious liberty or firearms were found.
candidates.description: Elkhart communications professional and military veteran making his third Libertarian run for the 2nd District (2022, 2024, 2026).

candidates.name: Kelly Thompson
candidates.gradeNote: Ballotpedia lists her affiliations as including Planned Parenthood and the ACLU; her platform calls for Medicare for All and a new tax on Wall Street trades to fund education. No stated positions on firearms or religious liberty were found.
candidates.description: Concrete contractor, nonprofit founder and former jail-ministry visiting pastor from North Webster; 2020 Democratic nominee for Indiana House District 22.

candidates.name: Marlin A. Stutzman
candidates.gradeNote: SBA Pro-Life America A+; Heritage Action 119th Congress score 100%; LCV lifetime 4%. Voted for the 2025 Born-Alive Abortion Survivors Protection Act and the 2025 Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act; platform emphasizes cutting federal spending, border security, gun rights and limiting the federal role in education.
candidates.description: Howe farmer and business owner, former Indiana House and Senate member, who returned to Congress in 2024 after previously holding the seat.

candidates.name: Drew Cox
candidates.gradeNote: Ballotpedia survey states he supports codifying Roe v. Wade and passing the Equality Act, calls for abolishing ICE, higher taxes on the ultra-wealthy and reduced military spending; he also states that removing the right to bear arms has no place in a free political system.
candidates.description: Purdue University music instructor and Marine Corps veteran (2008-2012) from Lafayette.

candidates.name: Jim Baird
candidates.gradeNote: SBA Pro-Life America A+; Heritage Action 119th Congress score 84%; LCV lifetime 6%. Voted against the 2022 Respect for Marriage Act and for the Born-Alive Abortion Survivors Protection Act (2023 and 2025) and the 2025 Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act.
candidates.description: Farmer, small-business owner and Vietnam veteran seeking a fifth term; former Putnam County commissioner and Indiana state representative.

candidates.name: J.D. Ford
candidates.gradeNote: As a state senator, voted against SB 1, Indiana's 2022 abortion ban (July 2022 Senate vote), and said he would 'strongly oppose' it; supports codifying Roe v. Wade federally and criticized the 2025 federal tax-and-spending package. Other state votes on the six values were not reviewed.
candidates.description: Indiana state senator for District 29 since 2018 and the first openly gay member of the Indiana General Assembly.

candidates.name: Victoria Spartz
candidates.gradeNote: SBA Pro-Life America A+; Heritage Action 119th Congress score 92%; LCV lifetime 4%. Voted against the 2022 Respect for Marriage Act and for the Born-Alive Abortion Survivors Protection Act (2023 and 2025); she was one of two Republicans to vote against the September 2025 stopgap spending bill.
candidates.description: Republican who has represented Indiana's 5th District since 2021 and won a third term in 2024.

candidates.name: Cynthia (Cinde) Wirth
candidates.gradeNote: Wirth has no legislative record; in a 2024 WFYI interview she backed Congress enshrining abortion protections, calling abortion "a health care procedure," and supported stronger gun background checks, and a Take Back Congress profile lists "protecting reproductive freedom" in her platform. She did not answer the iVoterGuide questionnaire, which rates her Liberal from public data, and her listed endorsements include the AFL-CIO and Progressive Voters Network.
candidates.description: Columbus-based small-business owner, scientist and former public high school biology teacher who was the 2024 Democratic nominee against Shreve.

candidates.name: Jefferson Shreve
candidates.gradeNote: Shreve holds an A+ from SBA Pro-Life America, which endorsed his re-election, and a 96% Heritage Action score for the 119th Congress; his platform includes abortion restrictions, gun rights, border security and reduced spending. As a 2023 Indianapolis mayoral candidate he proposed ending permitless carry, raising the gun-purchase age to 21 and banning assault-weapon sales in Marion County, a departure from the GOP line on the Second Amendment.
candidates.description: First-term Republican congressman, self-storage business founder and former Indianapolis City-County councilor who ran unsuccessfully for Indianapolis mayor in 2023.

candidates.name: André Carson
candidates.gradeNote: Carson holds an F from SBA Pro-Life America, which says he has consistently voted against protections for the unborn and children born alive after failed abortions, and a 0% Heritage Action score for the 119th Congress (7% lifetime). He voted Yea on final passage of the Respect for Marriage Act (Roll Call 513, Dec. 8, 2022).
candidates.description: Democratic congressman representing Indianapolis since a 2008 special election, Indiana's longest-serving current U.S. House member.

candidates.name: Patrick McAuley
candidates.gradeNote: McAuley has no voting record, and his campaign issues page covers only public safety, housing and job training; in a WFYI interview he called federal appropriations "a mess," proposed cutting overlapping humanitarian aid accounts and supported voter ID, while saying he is "completely open" to immigrants and criticizing ICE tactics. No public positions on abortion, marriage, religious liberty or guns were found, and iVoterGuide lists him as Insufficient Information.
candidates.description: Republican nominee who works in commercial real estate and previously interned for U.S. Sen. Todd Young.

candidates.name: James M Sceniak
candidates.gradeNote: Sceniak told WFYI he wants lower taxes for individuals, backs the "Penny Plan" to trim federal budgets and calls inflation a tax, while describing a welcoming "Reagan" view on immigration. He did not answer iVoterGuide's questions on life, marriage, religious liberty or guns, and iVoterGuide rates him Moderate.
candidates.description: Libertarian behavior therapist and repeat congressional candidate (2022 U.S. Senate, 2024 6th District) with no campaign website.

candidates.name: Mary Allen
candidates.gradeNote: Allen has no federal record; her campaign priorities call for the wealthy and corporations to "pay their fair share in taxes," more funding for USAID and public schools, opposition to dismantling the Department of Education, and immigration pathways to citizenship. She did not answer iVoterGuide's questions on life, marriage, religious liberty or guns, and iVoterGuide rates her Liberal from public data.
candidates.description: At-large Evansville City Council member, small-business owner, Army Reserve veteran and former occupational therapist.

candidates.name: Mark Messmer
candidates.gradeNote: Messmer holds an A+ from SBA Pro-Life America for votes including defunding Planned Parenthood through H.R. 1, and a 96% Heritage Action score for the 119th Congress. As Indiana Senate majority leader in 2022 he voted against SB 1, the near-total abortion ban, in committee, saying every anti-abortion organization he talked to had urged a no vote.
candidates.description: First-term Republican congressman from Jasper, small-business owner, and former Indiana Senate majority leader and state representative.

candidates.name: Brad A. Meyer
candidates.gradeNote: Meyer has no legislative record; his campaign advocates Medicare for All and stronger collective bargaining, and he told the Capital Chronicle he would make the first $20,000 in wages tax-free. He did not answer any iVoterGuide questions, which rates him Liberal from public data, and his listed endorsements include the AFL-CIO and Progressive Voters Network.
candidates.description: Democratic nominee and Bloomington electronics engineer whose career includes manufacturing and civilian engineering work for the U.S. Navy.

candidates.name: Erin Houchin
candidates.gradeNote: Houchin holds an A+ from SBA Pro-Life America, which notes she introduced the Abortion Funding Awareness Act and voted to defund Planned Parenthood through H.R. 1, and a 94% Heritage Action score for the 119th Congress (80% lifetime). Her platform emphasizes border security, reduced federal spending, abortion restrictions and parental involvement in education.
candidates.description: Republican congresswoman from Salem seeking a third term, a former Indiana state senator.

candidates.name: Tonya L. Hudson
candidates.gradeNote: In iVoterGuide answers Hudson agreed human life deserves legal protection from conception, strongly opposed taxpayer funding for abortion providers, opposed any new gun restrictions, opposed compelling businesses to provide services against their beliefs, and backed spending cuts, a balanced budget and abolishing the IRS. She strongly disagreed with defining marriage as one man and one woman and said anyone not dangerous should be allowed to migrate, though her campaign site calls for securing the southern border.
candidates.description: Libertarian real estate broker from Mitchell who previously ran for the 9th District seat in 2020 and 2022 and for lieutenant governor.
